tip: Weather questions use какая (kakaya = what kind), agreeing with feminine погода (pogoda = weather), where English just says how.
обычно (obychno = usually) takes the imperfective писали (pisali = wrote), stressing a repeated habit, not one finished paper.
сразу (srazu = at once) marks a finished action, so the perfective написал (napisal = wrote) is used, not the process form писал (pisal).
наконец (nakonets = finally) points to a result, so the perfective сделали (sdelali = did) is used, not the ongoing делали (delali).
Past verbs agree with the subject's gender: feminine она (ona) takes строила (stroila = built) with -ла, while a man would say строил (stroil).
отвечать (otvechat = to answer) pairs with на (na) plus the accusative: отвечала на письмо (otvechala na pismo = answered the letter).
забыть (zabyt = to forget) takes о (o) about something, which becomes об (ob) before a vowel: забыла об этом (zabyla ob etom = forgot about it).
Leaving a person uses от (ot = from) plus the genitive: ушла от подруги (ushla ot podrugi = left her friend).
Cold has no subject here: холодно (kholodno = cold) is an adverb form used for weather and how a place feels.
Needing something puts the person in the dative: мне (mne = to me) plus понадобится (ponadobitsya = will be needed), literally to-me it will be needed.
весь день (ves den = all day) describes duration, so the imperfective писал (pisal = was writing) is used, not the finished написал (napisal).
чтобы (chtoby = in order to) plus an infinitive shows purpose: чтобы понять (chtoby ponyat = in order to understand).
Repeated round trips use the multidirectional ходила (khodila = went), not the one-way шла (shla), so часто ходила (chasto khodila) means going there again and again.
After numbers from five up, the noun goes to genitive plural: пятнадцать минут (pyatnadtsat minut = fifteen minutes), not минуты (minuty).
Going to a person uses к (k = to) plus the dative: к врачу (k vrachu = to the doctor), where places take в (v) or на (na).
The receiver of дал (dal = gave) stands in the dative: своему брату (svoemu bratu = to my brother).
Playing a game uses играть (igrat) plus в (v) and the accusative: играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess).
каждое утро (kazhdoye utro = every morning) signals a habit, so the multidirectional плавали (plavali = swam) fits regular swims.
бегали (begali = ran around) is the multidirectional form for running in all directions, not toward one goal like бегут (begut).
Сколько бы он ни (skolko by on ni = no matter how much) makes a concession: however much he works, it is never enough.
Unreal past uses если бы (esli by = if) with a past verb, then бы again: мы бы не опоздали (my by ne opozdali = we would not have been late).
помогать (pomogat = to help) governs the dative, not the accusative: помогает другу (pomogayet drugu = helps a friend).
Repeated losing uses the imperfective терял (teryal = lost): постоянно терял (postoyanno teryal) marks it happening over and over.
A single completed loss uses the perfective потерял (poteryal = lost), formed by adding по- to терял (teryal).
Motion toward one goal uses the unidirectional бегут (begut = are running): бегут на площадку (begut na ploshchadku = running to the playground) means heading there now.
лучший (luchshiy = best) is the irregular superlative of good, standing in for a regular form like самый хороший (samyy khoroshiy).
Repeated trips by vehicle use the multidirectional ездил (yezdil = went): часто ездил (chasto yezdil) means going there regularly, round trip.
водил (vodil = took) is the multidirectional form for leading someone somewhere repeatedly, unlike the one-way ведёт (vedyot).
везёт (vezyot = is taking) is the unidirectional form for transporting by vehicle in progress, right now toward one place.
ведёт (vedyot = is leading) is the unidirectional form for taking someone on foot to one place now, unlike repeated водит (vodit).
Means of transport uses на (na = on) plus the prepositional: на поезде (na poezde = by train).
The more, the more pairs чем (chem) with тем (tem): чем больше читаешь, тем умнее (chem bolshe chitaesh, tem umneye = the more you read, the smarter).
In compound years only the last word takes the ordinal ending: девяносто первый (devyanosto pervyy = ninety first), earlier parts stay cardinal.
Traveling by car uses на (na = on) plus the prepositional: на машине (na mashine = by car).
так и не (tak i ne = never did) plus a perfective marks a planned action that never got done: так и не доделали (tak i ne dodelali = never finished it).
Imperfective учил (uchil = studied) names the effort; perfective выучил (vyuchil = learned) names the result, here denied by так и не (tak i ne).
The tool used takes the instrumental with no preposition: молотком и зубилом (molotkom i zubilom = with hammer and chisel).
A perfective in present form means future: помоет (pomoyet = will wash) refers to tomorrow, with no separate will word.
достичь (dostich = to reach) governs the genitive, not the accusative: достиг вершины (dostig vershiny = reached the summit).
